package.name: Url
package.description: URLs: parsing, normalizing and resolving them, and reading and building their queries

modules.name: Error
modules.header: Why text is not a URL, or why a URL could not be built.

modules.name: Normalize
modules.header:
Putting each component in the one form two equivalent URLs share, following section 6.2.2 of RFC 3986.
Percent-encoded octets are written with upper-case hexadecimal, and those that encode an unreserved character are
written as the character itself. A character a component cannot hold as itself — a space, a non-ASCII byte — is
percent-encoded rather than refused, as browsers do. The scheme and a registered host name are lower-cased, an IPv4
host keeps its dotted form, an IPv6 host is written in the canonical form of RFC 5952, and dot segments are removed
from the path.

modules.name: Parts
modules.header:
Cutting a URL or a relative reference into its components, without judging them yet.
The cut follows the regular expression in appendix B of RFC 3986, which every reference matches: a scheme before the
first `:` that comes before any `/`, `?` or `#`; an authority after `//`; a path up to `?` or `#`; a query up to
`#`; and a fragment after it. The authority is then cut into user information before its last `@`, a host, which
is bracketed when it is an IPv6 address, and a port after the host's `:`. Judging each component — which
characters it may hold, whether its host and port are well formed — is left to composing the URL from them.

modules.name: Query
modules.header:
Reading a query as `name=value` pairs, building one, and decoding a percent-encoded component into text.
A query is read as HTML forms write it: pairs separated by `&`, a name and a value separated by the first `=`, and
`+` standing for a space. The pairs come out still encoded, so nothing allocates until a caller decodes one.

modules.name: Url
modules.header:
A URL held in its normalized text, with where each component sits in it.
Parsing and resolving both end in composing a URL from pieces of text: the scheme is checked and lower-cased, the
authority's user information, host and port are checked and normalized, and the path, query and fragment are put in
normal form, with dot segments removed from the path. What comes out is ASCII, and two URLs that RFC 3986 calls
equivalent under syntax-based normalization come out as the same text, so comparing them is comparing text.

cases.name: MissingScheme
cases.doc: The text has no scheme, so it is a relative reference that needs a base to resolve against.

cases.name: InvalidScheme
cases.doc: The scheme does not start with a letter or holds a character a scheme cannot.

cases.name: InvalidHost
cases.doc: The host is empty where one is required, holds a character a host cannot, or is a malformed IPv6 address.

cases.name: InvalidPort
cases.doc: The port is not a number from 0 to 65535.

cases.name: InvalidPercentEncoding
cases.doc: A `%` is not followed by two hexadecimal digits.

cases.name: OutOfMemory
cases.doc: The allocator could not supply the storage.

cases.name: InvalidText
cases.doc: Decoded bytes are not UTF-8 text.

doc.summary: An absolute URL in normalized form.
doc.markdown:
An absolute URL in normalized form.
Read it with `Parse` and resolve references against it with `Resolve`. Every component is a view of the URL's own
text, still percent-encoded; `Decode` turns one into text. Copying a URL copies its text.

doc.summary: Reads `text` as an absolute URL and puts it in normalized form.
doc.markdown:
Reads `text` as an absolute URL and puts it in normalized form.
Spaces and control characters around the text are ignored. A character a component cannot hold as itself,
such as a space or a non-ASCII byte, is percent-encoded; a host is not, and refuses one.

doc.summary:
Resolves `reference` against this URL, as a browser resolves a link on a page, following section 5 of

doc.markdown:
Resolves `reference` against this URL, as a browser resolves a link on a page, following section 5 of
RFC 3986. An absolute reference stands on its own; `//host/path`, `/path`, `path`, `?query` and `#fragment`
replace what they name and keep the rest of this URL.

params.markdown: an absolute URL or a relative reference
